edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia (archive bub_gb_DY2xvRwPetMC), Latin column, Duodecim Capita de Fide, Cap. VIII, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 29)

source_text: Si quis dicit, perfectum hominem esse Christum divise, et Deum Verbum divise; et non confitetur unum Dominum Iesum Christum, sicut scriptum est; anathema sit. Quomodo dicere quis potest perfectum hominem Christum divise, et Deum Verbum divise; cum ipse Dominus dicat: Quid me quaeritis occidere hominem, qui veritatem loquutus sum, quam audivi a patre? Non enim hominem pro nobis dedit, sed se ipsum pro nobis tradidit Deus Verbum homo propter nos factum. Quapropter dicit: Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud. Ipse autem dicebat de templo corporis sui.
thought_title: Christ is not divided into a perfect man and God the Word
orientation: Gregory condemns dividing Christ into a perfect man and God the Word, since the one Word made man gave himself for us.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says Christ [is] a perfect man (perfectum hominem) separately (divise), and God the Word (Deum Verbum) separately; and does not confess one Lord Jesus Christ, as it is written; let him be anathema. How can anyone say Christ [is] a perfect man separately, and God the Word separately; when the Lord himself says: Why do you seek to kill me, a man (hominem), who have spoken (loquutus sum) the truth (veritatem) which I heard from the father? For not a man did he give (dedit) for us, but himself (se ipsum) he handed over (tradidit) for us, God the Word made man (homo factum) on account of us. Wherefore he says: Destroy (solvite) this temple (templum), and in three days I will raise (excitabo) it. But he was speaking of the temple of his body (corporis).

pass_b_english: If anyone says that Christ is a perfect man separately, and God the Word separately, and does not confess one Lord Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 8:6), as it is written, let him be anathema.

How can anyone say that Christ is a perfect man separately and God the Word separately, when the Lord himself says, “Why do you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth that I heard from the Father?” (John 7:19; John 8:40) For God the Word, made man for our sake, did not give a man for us, but handed himself over for us. That is why he says, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up” (John 2:19). But he was speaking of the temple of his body (John 2:21).
notes: Divise (“separately”) is the key term: the rejected view counts the man and the Word as two.

The quoted saying blends John 7:19 (quid me quaeritis interficere) with John 8:40, which reads “from God” where this text has “from the Father”; the reading of this text is translated, and both verses are cited inline.
“He handed himself over for us” echoes Ephesians 5:2, Galatians 2:20 and Titus 2:14 (dedit semetipsum pro nobis); no single verse is certain, so it is left uncited.
“One Lord Jesus Christ” is cited to 1 Corinthians 8:6 because the anathema says “as it is written”.
